item.title: Rays on the verge of ensuring ultra-rare World Series phenomenon
item.description: Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Rays on the verge of ensuring ultra-rare World Series phenomenon appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays are being pushed to their limit by the Cleveland Guardians. Nonetheless, over the past two days, the Rays have shown why they were the best team in the AL this past season. After falling down 2-1 in the ALCS, the Rays have bounced back with two consecutive victories on the road — with Tampa Bay having taken a 3-2 lead in the series courtesy of a 3-1 win on Sunday. With that victory, the Rays are now knocking on the door of the World Series, where the Milwaukee Brewers await. It seems like the postponement of Friday night’s contest due to inclement weather helped them immensely, as Game 6 (as well as Game 7, if necessary) will be at Tropicana Field — giving Tampa Bay a golden opportunity to secure their third appearance in the Fall Classic. Moreover, if the Rays were to win another game against the Guardians in the ALCS, they would ensure a rare World Series phenomenon with the Milwaukee Brewers already waiting on the other side of the bracket. As per Rays insider Steve Carney, if Tampa Bay were to advance to the next round, this would be the first World Series matchup in 46 years between two teams that have never won a title. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In 1980, the Kansas City Royals and Philadelphia Phillies faced off against each other for a chance to win their first World Series title. In the end, it was the Phillies that got the better of the Royals, winning the series 4-2. The Royals would get their breakthrough in 1985 and would follow that up with another title in 2015. The Brewers, like the Rays, have been in the World Series before. However, Milwaukee has only had just one shot at winning a title, and they whiffed it back in 1982 — losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals. Meanwhile, the Rays have made it to the Fall Classic twice, falling to the Phillies and the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2008 and 2020, respectively. Can they make it three World Series appearances for the franchise with a win either on Monday night or on Tuesday (if necessary)? item.title: Nashville SC Locks Up 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup Spot
item.description: Nashville SC Locks Up 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup Spot Nashville SC is the first MLS club to clinch a spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. The team has guaranteed a finish no worse than third in the league's overall standings, with matches still remaining on the 2026 schedule. The math is simple: Nashville's position is now unreachable by any chasing club, even in a worst-case run to close out the season. That removes any dependency on other results and hands the front office an international fixture to plan around a year in advance. What's next for Nashville Qualification doesn't end the ambition. Third place is the floor, not the ceiling, and Nashville still has reason to push for a higher finish before the playoffs begin. A stronger regular-season position carries weight heading into the postseason, where seeding and momentum matter. The early clinch also gives the roster-building process a head start. Playing continental and domestic competitions at once demands depth — injuries, suspensions and fatigue all hit harder across a packed calendar — so locking in the Champions Cup spot now lets the front office plan accordingly instead of waiting on the regular season's final weeks. Why the Champions Cup matters The Concacaf Champions Cup is the region's top club competition, pitting MLS sides against teams from Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. For Nashville, it's a chance to test the squad against different styles and raise its profile beyond the domestic league — part of a broader push by MLS clubs to build credibility on the continental stage.

item.title: How Notre Dame’s opponents fared in WEEK 7 of the CFB season
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS - OCTOBER 17: Miami defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald (3) intercepts an FSU pass to the end zone in overtime to end the game (also pictured, defensive back Dylan Day (23), defensive back Damari Brown (2), defensive back Omar Thornton (0); Florida State wide receiver Micahi Danzy (8), wide receiver Jayvan Boggs (15)) the Miami Hurricanes faced the Florida State Seminoles on October 17, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Notre Dame’s 2026 college football schedule has been called many thing over the last eight months, but “tough” or anywhere near the word “hard” was certainly not among them. Still, some have mentioned that this Irish schedule could look a lot trickier as the season progresses. While they may eventually be true, it may not matter all that much (except for message boards and social media). Notre Dame took a minute or two to get going against the Wisconsin Badgers in the season opener, but eventually the Irish whooped them 42-13. Notre Dame welcomed the Rice Owls to South Bend for the home opener, and sent them back to Texas with a 52-0 loss. Although the Irish were big favorites against Michigan State, they got their best shot — and still beat the Spartans 27-10. The Irish were once again massive favorites over a Big 10 team, and they more than covered against Purdue with a 49-10 win that was never that close. Notre Dame was better than a three touchdown favorite against North Carolina, but ran into a bit of a clunker (and rain) and beat the Tar Heels 37-26. After two weeks on the road, Notre Dame returned to South Bend and the homecooking did them well as the Irish destroyed the Stanford Cardinal 58-7. Disaster hit the Irish against BYU in a 28-24 loss, and no matter what part of the game you want to complain about (because there was quite a bit) the simplest thing to say is that Notre Dame flat out got outplayed by the Cougars. Notre Dame will now be able to chomp down some cheeseburgers during their bye week. Notre Dame is still likely to be favored in every game this season, and they are still a popular pick to win the national championship. Their strength of schedule probably isn’t going to matter much, but let’s keep track of it anyway. item.title: Messi Heads to Spain for Asturias Award, Eyes Miami Return
item.description: Messi Heads to Spain for Asturias Award, Eyes Miami Return Lionel Messi will fly to Spain on October 22 to receive the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first soccer player ever to win the honor. Inter Miami expects him back in time for the club's MLS clash with the New York Red Bulls two days later. The award, announced back in June, recognizes standout figures across sports, culture, science and international cooperation. The selection committee cited not just Messi's trophy haul but his influence on the global growth of the game. Quick turnaround for Red Bulls clash Coach González said the club fully supports Messi's trip to Oviedo, calling the tribute meaningful for the player and his family. Despite the short window, Miami is confident its captain will be ready for the October 24 match in Harrison, New Jersey. Inter Miami has already clinched a playoff berth, but the matchup still matters. item.title: NFL Could Hand Down Punishment Over Rams Game After Controversial Call
item.description: Sean McVay and the Rams could see the NFL step in over Josh Wallace's unnecessary roughness penalty. Getty The Los Angeles Rams’ loss to the Arizona Cardinals featured a polarizing call against cornerback Josh Wallace that could see the NFL step in. Unfortunately for Wallace and the Rams, further discipline is among the possible outcomes. On a first-and-10 play from the Cardinals 35-yard line, Arizona’s Jacoby Brissett connected with wide receiver Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard gain. As he came down with the pass, Wallace was attempting to make the tackle, but connected with Brooks’ helmet instead. It was a blow from the shoulder. Officials still flagged Wallace for “unnecessary roughness,” gifting the Cardinals 15 yards, putting them within field goal range. There was also an offsides call against Josaiah Stewart, but the Cardinals, naturally, declined. Rams’ Josh Wallace Could Be Punished By NFL During the game, rules analyst Mike Pereira sided with the broadcast team that the hit did not seem to meet the criteria for a flag, i.e. forcible contact to the head and or neck area. But Wallace must now be concerned that the NFL will side with the officials. Wallace’s hit could see the infraction specified as a “hit on a defenseless player.” That is one of the NFL’s fineable offenses. Per the NFL , a first-time infraction can incur a fine as high as $17,911. A second infraction could draw a fine as high as $23,882. This infraction would also count as one strike for Wallace. Two more strikes of this kind, and the third-year cornerback will trigger an automatic one-game suspension. Wallace can appeal the fine, potentially leading to a reduction. However, the strike will carry over into future seasons if it holds. To make matters worse, that was the only penalty called for a fineable offense in the game. Reactions to Rams Penalty Telling Wallace was also on the wrong side of a call against the Rams that altered their loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 3. He could see history repeat itself in that regard, but the Rams are feeling that in-game decision now. “UNREAL PERSONAL FOUL,” Sharp Football Analysis’ Warren Sharp posted on X in reaction to the call, including a clip. “WHAT DO YOU WANT HIM TO DO???” Rams On SI’s Blaine Grisak posted , “How are we calling that unnecessary roughness on Josh Wallace?” adding that is was “another penalty this season late in the fourth quarter that Wallace has been screwed on.” “Another tough call on Josh Wallace there, and I don’t love it, but the Rams put themselves in this position to lose this game,” Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer posted on X. Former NFL safety Quandre Diggs posted on X that the “Rams got cheated.” Rivals’ Greg Biggins posted , “The League obviously hates Josh Wallace! What a wild way to lose a game [laughing face emoji],” underscoring the incredulous response to the call that many had in real time. Wallace was playing so much partly due to the absence of Trent McDuffie. McDuffie suffered a groin injury

item.title: Buffalo Bills Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson Breaks Silence on Ejection
item.description: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: C.J. Gardner-Johnson #22 of the Buffalo Bills gets his fingers taped up during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) Getty C.J. Gardner-Johnson apologized to Buffalo Bills. Getty The Buffalo Bills entered the bye week with a 33-31 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday afternoon. Before the first half ended, Bills starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected for spitting near a Raiders player. The play resulted in a 15-yard penalty and a chance for the Raiders to take one shot at the end zone. The Bills will enter their bye week with a record of 5-1. C.J. Gardner-Johnson Apologizes to Buffalo Bills Getty C.J. Gardner-Johnson apologized to Buffalo Bills. After the ejection, Gardner-Johnson did face the music as he spoke to the media after the game. Gardner-Johnson apologized to the team and said it was something he can’t do, as it hurts the team. “We were just arguing and talking,” Gardner-Johnson told reporters postgame . “It was nothing negative. He ain’t do nothing to me. It was just in the heat of the game arguing and talking s**t. That gesture isn’t warranted.” Gardner-Johnson said he does expect to be fined for it, and knows he has to be better going forward. “I got to be a better player, I got to be a better vet, I hurt my team,” Gardner-Johnson said. I just go to control my emotions.” Although Gardner-Johnson knows he has to be better, whether or not he gets a chance to prove that is unclear. There are calls for the Bills to cut him after the ejection, as he’s also struggled this season, which could lead to Damar Hamlin or Jalen Kilgore taking over his role. Joe Brady Sends Message to Gardner-Johnson Before Gardner-Johnson spoke to the media in the locker room, Joe Brady made his feelings clear about the ejection. Brady said it’s something the Bills will address and is something they can’t allow. “I haven’t seen the clip yet. I was talking to the ref, they took it to New York and it was clear as day. I’m sure I’m going to see it shortly after here. At the end of the day, if it shows up, that can’t happen; that’s the discipline I’m talking about. It’s uncalled for, it can’t happen, and it’s going to be addressed,” Brady said . Whether or not the Bills will move on from Gardner-Johnson is to be seen. But the team can use the bye week as a chance to bring in some safeties and perhaps take his job. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Buffalo Bills Safety C.J. item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Chargers’ Tony Jefferson drops defiant take amid brutal 0-6 situation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Chargers continue to sink further in the 2026 season. Now the Kansas City Chiefs dropped them to 0-6 following the 22-6 loss at Arrowhead Stadium. But Tony Jefferson dropped a defiant take. The safety doesn’t believe his team is dead in the water yet. “Until they say we’re dead, we’re alive. So we’re just gonna keep fighting,” Jefferson said to reporters. “Nobody’s going to lay down or quit.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Until they say we're dead, we're alive. So we're just gonna keep fighting." Tony Jefferson is doing his best to stay hopeful as the Chargers drop to 0-6. #boltup | @CBSLosAngeles pic.twitter.com/ww6aoLeDx3 — Sports Central LA (@SportsCentralLA) October 19, 2026 The Chargers and coach Jim Harbaugh will love that kind of confidence from one of their veteran leaders. But the Chargers are teetering towards finishing with their worst mark since the 2000 season. That Bolts team ended up going 1-15, and that was the last time LAC started 0-6. So this is the first worst start in the Harbaugh regime. Many point to Harbaugh not meshing with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel as a big reason behind the slow start. Granted, Harbaugh has denied in the past that he wouldn’t take away the play-calling duties from McDaniel. Harbaugh’s postgame words, though, paint a different picture. “We have to address everything guys and especially offensively. We’re not scoring enough points,” Harbaugh said to reporters afterward. “We’re going to look at everything. The job I’m doing, it starts with me. The plan is we’ll watch this and get with our offensive coaches. … [Offense] Needs to be addressed.” So that paints the picture that Harbaugh and McDaniel may need to pivot to another direction offensively. Meanwhile on defense, Jefferson tallied five tackles and finished third there. But LAC allowed 422 total yards. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Shares Positive Update on Knee After Week 6 Win
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Linebacker Del'shawn Phillips #53 of the Los Angeles Chargers pulls down quarterback Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs in the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs remain undefeated in the 2026 season, having beaten the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6 to go 5-0. The Chiefs are the only unbeaten team in the AFC, alongside the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings make up the only teams to have not been bested yet in the NFL. Perhaps the even more impressive note to the Chiefs’ win-streak is the fact that quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off a serious knee injury back in December that saw him tear his ACL and LCL in his left knee. Patrick Mahomes Speaks on Knee Health After Chargers Win Mahomes was ready to start the year after making a quicker-than-expected recovery, and five games in has looked his best self in the regular season in almost half a decade. Speaking to the media after the win against the Chargers, the former two-time MVP shared how his knee was feeling as he continues to get closer to 100%. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes on his knee: "After the bye week, I felt better physically… There's still some burst I don't have… But that's something we'll continue to work on." — Charles Goldman (@goldmctNFL) October 19, 2026 “After the bye week, I felt better physically… There’s still some burst I don’t have… But that’s something we’ll continue to work on.” Mahomes said after the game, via Charles Goldman. Patrick Mahomes ‘Better’ Despite Not Having Full Burst Even though the 31-year old has been practicing since training camp and has yet to miss a game this season, his words make it clear that being on the field does not inherently imply a full bill of health in the National Football League. The exact timeline for Mahomes getting his burst back to what it was prior to the injury is unknown. And for players sustaining serious knee injuries after the age of 30, there is no guarantee he’ll ever be quite as fast as he was before. But him feeling improved and is certainly a positive for the team, and whilst Mahomes is an agile QB, him having game-breaking speed has never been major part of his game. item.title: Thunder’s Jaylin Williams makes wild request after Cason Wallace’s contract extension
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Thunder’s Jaylin Williams makes wild request after Cason Wallace’s contract extension appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma City Thunder opened up the brink trunks a few days before their season opener, agreeing to a contract extension with Cason Wallace worth five years and $139 million. It was the next highly anticipated extension for the franchise, especially given how Wallace has played over the past few years. Moments after the extension was announced, Wallace went on Instagram and made a post, and his teammates were quick to comment. Jaylin Williams was one of the first, and he had a wild request after Wallace got paid. “So you finna buy me you & K matching lambos,” Williams wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was a bold request from Williams, and there’s a good chance that since he’s not a family member, he won’t be getting any cars. If anything, Wallace is going to buy himself a car with the new money he has. It’s a well-deserved extension for Wallace, who is slated to be in the starting lineup this season after Lu Dort was traded to the Atlanta Hawks during the offseason. After his play last season and in the postseason, there were many people who expected that Wallace would see an increase in minutes this season, and even a larger role. Wallace is one of the better defenders on the team, as well as an average 3-point shooter. He’ll be playing more of the role that Dort had in the starting lineup, but Wallace has more shot creation in his game. Though the Thunder lost key pieces during the offseason like Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, they have enough depth on the team to fill their voids. It should be another good season for the team, especially with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren leading the way. item.title: Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski Gets Honest After Frustrating Loss to Bears
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Head coach Kevin Stefanski of the Atlanta Falcons looks on prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) Getty The Atlanta Falcons suffered their second straight loss by losing to the Chicago Bears 31-23. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams made his return after a three-game absence due to a hamstring. Williams showed no signs of rust by throwing for 305 yards and a touchdown against an impressive Falcons defense. The Falcons came in being the number one rushing defense in the league and the team did a decent job of stopping the run for the most part. “Williams was 12 of 12 for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion in the second quarter,” an ESPN article says. “Though the Bears won two of three games with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum filing in at quarterback, Williams’ return sparked the offense. He completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards with one touchdown.” Atlanta’s Slow Start Kevin Stefanski made it a focal point to start out fast against this Bears team. Unfortunately, it did not happen. “Instead, the visiting team raced out to a 14-0 lead in Mercedes-Benz Stadium,” Will McFadden wrote in an Atlanta Falcons article . “The Bears built that lead up to 31-7 on the first play of the fourth quarter, a cushion large enough to withstand a furious Falcons rally that nearly turned the game on its head in the final 10 minutes. Tight end Kyle Pitts caught two touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to close the gap, but Atlanta ran out of time and couldn’t overcome its slow start, losing 31-23.” Though Stefanski made it a focal point to start fast, as expected, he was not pleased with how the team started. It’s one thing to talk about it, it’s another thing to actually put it out on the field. “I’m obviously proud of how we continue to fight, but to start like we started is really, really disappointing,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said after the game . “That’s something we talked at length about, and we talked at length about starting fast in this ballgame, and we did not.” “We’ve got to get that fixed because we just put ourselves in the hole,” Stefanski said. “Disappointed. I’ll have to look at how we start and make sure that we are putting our guys in position, but we will own that one, and we will move on.” Atlanta Could Not Get The Run Game Going The identity of this Falcons team is to get Bijan Robinson and this run game going. Robinson was held to 61 yards on the ground, yet only carried the ball nine times. “That’s what we set our identity in: this run game,” Robinson said after the game . “The run game gets everything going on this offense. So, for us, I know when we got down those scores, we were trying to play catch-up with the passes, so we could try to get as many yards as we can. item.title: ‘He is not human’ – NFL fans cannot believe Josh Allen’s ‘miracle play’ in big win
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images One Josh Allen masterclass moment has captured the attention of NFL fans after the Buffalo Bills’ big win and most are simply awestruck by his genius. In what proved to be a tight contest against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Buffalo Bills claimed their fifth win of the season. The difference-maker was none other than the team’s star quarterback. Josh Allen did just enough to secure the victory for his team. Allen threw the ball for 255 yards and two touchdowns, and looked like his usual impressive self during the game. The 33-30 scoreline suggests how tight the game was. And while a game like this is generally known for having a lot of big moments, one Allen play has really captured the fans’ imaginations. Josh Allen’s third quarter scramble and touchdown pass left NFL fans online in awe of his skills With the score at 16-13 in the third quarter, Allen had the ball for the Bills at the Raiders’ 13-yard line. It was third down with eight yards to gain, and it would have been bad for Buffalo if they had to settle for the field goal. The Raiders’ defensive line knew they had to get the stop if they could. They sold out to try to sack Allen, but he somehow escaped the pocket. As more Las Vegas players rushed to meet him and put him on the ground, the 30-year-old casually flipped the ball to Keon Coleman in the endzone. “Josh Allen is something else man, he is not human,” one fan wrote. “Josh Allen is the 6th grader playing with 4th graders at recess,” a second fan observed. “Josh Allen is not human. This is a new level of excellence we are not worthy of,” said a third fan. “I feel like even Josh Allen is surprised by the things Josh Allen can do sometimes,” a fourth fan hilariously claimed. “Give him the MVP right now,” a different comment read. “He can do anything. And his receivers know that at any moment he might do something nuts, so they’re always ready. It’s a pleasure to watch that man apply his craft,” a sixth fan said. The vision to see that play and the talent to make it are unfathomable for most quarterbacks, even at the highest level. Allen is making a strong case for himself to be named MVP for the second time in his career, and the fans clearly think he is the best around at the moment. item.title: Kirk Herbstreit Breaks Silence on Controversial Notre Dame-BYU Ending
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Kirk Herbstreit walks the field prior to the game during a game between the Denver Broncos and the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) Getty The No. 2 Notre Dame Fighting Irish lost in dramatic fashion to the No. 8 BYU Cougars on Saturday night. Notre Dame trailed 28-24 and had the ball at first-and-goal with just four seconds remaining on the clock. Star quarterback CJ Carr threw an incomplete pass on a play that appeared to involve pass interference. However, officials called the game over without checking whether any time remained on the clock. View this post on Instagram Big 12 Releases Statement on Final Play Just hours after the game, the Big 12 released a statement acknowledging that officials should have put one second back on the clock after Carr’s incomplete pass. That would have given Notre Dame another opportunity to reach the end zone on second-and-goal. “It was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew,” the Big 12’s statement read . “The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week’s games.” The Big 12 released a statement following its review of the ending of Notre Dame-BYU that one second should have been put back on the clock after the game’s final play, which resulted in a 28-24 BYU win, while the Irish had possession. “It was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew. The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week’s games.” — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 18, 2026 Kirk Herbstreit Speaks on Notre Dame-BYU Game Kirk Herbstreit, who called the game alongside Chris Fowler for ESPN on ABC, shared his thoughts on the finish and BYU’s impressive performance on social media Sunday afternoon. “Another week, another wild finish! A lot of talk about the ending, but let’s not lose sight of what BYU did to put themselves in position to win this ballgame,” Herbstreit said. “Tremendous effort by the Cougars to find a way to get it done. And of course don’t count Notre Dame out… Still a lot of football left to be played!” Herbstreit’s takes on Notre Dame haven’t been well received by the fanbase, especially after he recently criticized the team’s schedule. However, he picked the Fighting Irish as his preseason national champion and has stood by that prediction. item.title: Bills HC Joe Brady in awe of rookie’s ‘stickiness’ in win vs. Raiders
item.description: Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images Bills HC Joe Brady in awe of rookie’s ‘stickiness’ in win vs. Raiders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills returned to the winning column after suffering their first loss of the season, handing the Las Vegas Raiders a 33-30 loss in Week 6 of the NFL season. While the spotlight largely remained on Josh Allen and James Cook for their heroic performances, Bills head coach Joe Brady made sure to highlight rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun’s ‘stickiness’ in coverage following the win. During his postgame press conference, Brady praised Igbinosun’s ability to remain close to opposing receivers and continue competing regardless of the outcome of individual plays. “We were a little matchier today in coverage, and the stickiness kind of showed, and that’s what IGB kind of does,” Brady said. “And what I love about IGB is he just keeps playing, and they might take a shot, and he’s going to go right back at it with the same mindset.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He has a short memory, and so he’s continuing to grow game in game out and us getting a feel for what’s best for him, but one thing I know is he competes every damn play, and that’s exactly what we’re looking for.” Igbinosun delivered a notable performance against the Raiders, recording three pass deflections and two total tackles in Buffalo’s narrow victory. The second-round pick out of Ohio State registered one solo tackle and one assisted tackle while helping the Bills disrupt Las Vegas’ passing attack. The rookie’s performance provided an encouraging sign for Buffalo’s secondary as the team looks to maintain its strong start to the season. The victory improved Buffalo’s record to 5-1 this season. However, the game was not without controversy for the Bills. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the first half . The win gives Brady’s team additional momentum heading into its bye week. The Bills will have an opportunity to rest and address areas for improvement before hosting the Baltimore Ravens. item.title: Florida HC Jon Sumrall Explains Why Gators ‘Still Suck’ After Texas Win
item.description: Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall explained why he thinks the Gators still suck, despite the Texas win. Getty It’s been a rollercoaster of a first season for Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall. Going into Saturday’s game, it looked like the Gators were in freefall. With a road trip to play the Texas Longhorns, a favorite to make the College Football Playoff, it seemed like things would only get worse. Then, Florida pulled off a massive upset and came from behind to knock off Texas. All of a sudden, Sumrall and the Gators are trending up again. In the 27-24 win, Florida turned to Tramell Jones as their starting quarterback. He was limited, only throwing for 155 yards and 2 touchdowns, but he also made winning plays, like scrambling for a first down late on a read option. Then, the defense came up big, with 5 sacks and a forced fumble to help put the game on ice. Florida Gators HC Jon Sumrall Says They Still Suck There was, obviously, plenty to like from Florida on Saturday. There were still things to work on. That’s what Jon Sumrall tried to focus on, noting that he thinks that the Gators still suck. They might just suck a bit less now. “In this game or in life,” Sumrall said . “You don’t get to go, ‘Hey, I was good last week, so I get to be good next week, right?’ I guess part of why we got our ass kicked in Missouri and last week at home is because everybody around Gainesville was patting our guys in the back telling them how good they were, and I’m like, guys, we suck. Like I’ve watched this practice, we’re not very good. We still suck. We just suck less, all right. And so, we have to figure out to suck less each week.” The problem is that Florida still has some major issues to take care of. The secondary is susceptible to giving up big plays. The offense hasn’t been consistent, coming off two blowout losses in SEC play before the Texas win. Sumrall is being a bit harsh to say his team sucks. But his point is well taken. One great win doesn’t make you a great team. It makes you a team that had a great win. “But we’re not like a complete team yet. So, this does nothing for us. What it does for us, it gets us another win. item.title: Cason Wallace signs $139 million contract extension with OKC Thunder
item.description: Former Kentucky Wildcats standout Cason Wallace is staying in Oklahoma City, as Shams Charania reports that Wallace signed a five-year, $139 million rookie-scale contract extension with the Thunder. Wallace has been a valuable piece for the Thunder since being drafted in the first round in 2023. Last year, coming off the bench for the Thunder, Wallace averaged 8.6 points per game to go along with 3.1 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game. However, Wallace’s value has consistently been on the defensive side of the ball, where he has averaged almost two steals per game the last two seasons and has been one of OKC’s most reliable perimeter defenders and one of the best perimeter defenders in the league, as evidenced by being named a member of the 2025-26 NBA All-Defensive Second Team. After some offseason moves, including trading Luguentz Dort to the Atlanta Hawks, Wallace is expected to see an expanded role with the Thunder, and it’s clear from this contract extension that the Thunder see Wallace as a key piece to the team long-term. item.title: Packers' Defense Stifles Cowboys' Offense for Week 6 Win
item.description: The Green Bay Packers improved to 4-2 on the season with a 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. It wasn't Green Bay's best effort, as they had plenty of missed opportunities in the game, but they did enough to secure the win. Jordan Love finished the game completing 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. He also rushed for a touchdown on a quarterback sneak. Love's numbers could've been much better, as Matthew Golden dropped two touchdowns and Christian Watson dropped a touchdown. It was still a quality game from their top two weapons, as Golden had six receptions for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Watson had three receptions for 64 yards. Savion Williams also made an impact in the receiving game upon his return from injured reserve, catching four passes for 32 yards. Green Bay once again couldn't get anything going in the run game, as they rushed for 59 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries as a team (2.5 yards per carry). Love carried the offense, making a ton of great decisions and leading the offense on some productive drives. They could've scored more, as they had drops and penalties, but the Packers came away with the win. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The defense was the real story for Green Bay as they held Dallas to 13 points despite their talented offense led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Lamb finished with nine receptions for 70 yards, while Pickens had six receptions for 73 yards. Lamb and Pickens are one of the best receiving duos in the league, but the Packers were able to contain them. Jonathan Gannon's defense played at a high level, disguising their coverages and confusing Dak Prescott. Brandon Cisse and Evan Williams picked him off, while Lukas Van Ness sacked him once, and the team had seven quarterback hits. Green Bay's defensive backs were also very disruptive with eight pass deflections. The defense struggled with penalties, including three roughing-the-passer penalties, which could've proven costly. The Packers will need to clean that up, as teams will take advantage if it becomes a consistent issue. Rookie kicker Trey Smack was much better just a week after missing two field goals and an extra point. Smack made all three field goal attempts and both extra points in the win. Green Bay has some issues to clean up, but they should carry some momentum with their three-game winning streak into their matchup against the Detroit Lions next week.

item.title: Rays Take Control of ALCS With Gritty Game 5 Victory Over Guardians
item.description: Photo by: David Richard Tampa Bay Moves One Win Away From the World Series The Tampa Bay Rays are one win away from reaching the World Series after defeating the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 in Game 5 of the American League Championship Series on Sunday. Behind another outstanding postseason performance from starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen and timely hitting throughout the lineup, Tampa Bay took a 3-2 lead in the best of seven series. The Rays entered the matchup looking to build on Saturday’s 7-3 victory, which evened the series at two games apiece. They delivered another strong performance in Cleveland, putting themselves in position to clinch the American League pennant on their home field. Drew Rasmussen Delivers Another Strong Start Rasmussen was the biggest difference-maker Sunday, holding Cleveland to one run on four hits across seven innings. He consistently kept the Guardians’ hitters off balance, limiting scoring opportunities and giving Tampa Bay’s offense time to build an advantage. The outing continued Rasmussen’s impressive postseason run. His performance helped the Rays control the game from the early innings and put pressure on Cleveland to find answers against Tampa Bay’s pitching staff. Rasmussen’s ability to work deep into the game also protected the bullpen, allowing the Rays to turn the final two innings over to their relievers with a lead. Bryan Baker eventually closed out the victory, recording his fifth save of the postseason as Tampa Bay held off Cleveland’s late push. Rays Get Timely Contributions at the Plate Tampa Bay established control early, building a 3-0 advantage through the first three innings. Jonny DeLuca drove in the opening run, Jonathan Aranda added an RBI single, and Liam Hicks delivered another run scoring hit. item.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
